kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Project Most Complete Starter Kit

identity.manufacturer: unbranded / generic (no manufacturer markings printed on the part)
identity.manufacturer_part_number: not specified by ELEGOO, generic part; comparable retail part is SparkFun COM-08375
identity.package: ceramic disc, through-hole, radial leads, 0.1 in lead spacing

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A small capacitor that soaks up tiny, fast voltage bumps on a power line, usually placed right next to the chip that needs clean power.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Commonly called a decoupling or bypass capacitor. Placed as close as possible to the power pins of a chip, such as the ATmega328 on the UNO or any IC added on the breadboard, to absorb quick voltage spikes and switching noise so the chip runs reliably.
function.how_it_works_briefly: It is a small reservoir of charge that reacts almost instantly, much faster than a battery or a larger electrolytic capacitor. When a chip suddenly needs a brief burst of current, this capacitor supplies it locally instead of forcing the current to travel all the way back from the main power supply, which reduces noise and voltage dips.

pinout.name: Lead A
pinout.notes: Either lead can connect to either side of the circuit; no polarity.

pinout.name: Lead B
pinout.notes: Electrically identical to Lead A and interchangeable with it.

pins.pin_1_identification: Not applicable. There is no positive lead. Both leads are electrically identical and can be swapped without changing the circuit.

electrical.absolute_max_voltage: 50V DC (per SparkFun COM-08375; ELEGOO's exact unit is not independently datasheet-confirmed)
electrical.typical_current: not applicable, passive component with no intrinsic current draw

key_specs.marking_code: Printed as '104': the first two digits (10) are the significant figures, and the third digit (4) is the power-of-ten multiplier in picofarads, so 10 x 10^4 pF = 100,000 pF = 100 nF.

visual_identification.shape_and_size: A small flat disc, slightly larger than the 22pF part, roughly 5-7 mm across, with two straight wire leads about 0.1 inch apart.
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Body color varies by supplier, commonly blue or yellow/tan. Printed with '104'.
easily_confused_with: 22pF ceramic capacitor: same disc shape but marked '22' instead of '104' and usually a visibly smaller body
other 3-digit-coded ceramic capacitors such as 103 (10 nF) or 105 (1 uF), distinguished only by the printed number

example_connections.uno_pin: 5V or a chip's power pin, wired as close to the chip as possible
GND, forming a short path directly across the chip's power and ground pins

hazards: none under normal use within its 50V rating
handling_notes: keep lead lengths short when using it as a decoupling capacitor; long leads add inductance that reduces how well it filters fast noise
common_mistakes: confusing it with the visually similar 22pF capacitor since both are small ceramic discs
expecting it to smooth slow, large power dips the way a bigger electrolytic capacitor does; 100 nF only helps with fast, high-frequency noise

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: a chip resets randomly, glitches, or misbehaves only under load
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: missing decoupling capacitor, or one placed too far from the chip's power pins
symptoms_and_causes.check: confirm a 104 capacitor sits close to the chip's power pins; measure with a multimeter's capacitance mode and expect a reading close to 100 nF (often shown as 0.10 on a uF-range meter)

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: Set the multimeter to capacitance mode and read across the two leads; expect roughly 100 nF (0.1 uF).
